verdict: FICO's revenue jumped 27% to $657M on higher mortgage-score prices, but a $65M legal settlement accrual and a $27M restructuring charge held GAAP profit to $175M.

segments.name: Scores
segments.note: Credit scores sold to lenders and consumers — up 33%, mainly because the price per mortgage-origination score rose, even though mortgage volumes fell.

segments.name: Software
segments.note: Analytics and decisioning software: $223.7M of subscriptions and on-premises licenses plus $19.5M of professional services. Platform ARR grew 72%.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: The back office, sales and company-wide costs — this quarter it includes the $65M accrual for the proposed antitrust settlement.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building and improving the scoring and software products.

opex.name: Restructuring charges
opex.note: One-off cost of a committed workforce-reduction plan.

otherDetail: Other expense, net of $29.1M: mainly interest on FICO's debt, partly offset by a $47.9M gain on the sale of a minority equity investment.

takeaways.title: Score pricing is the growth engine
takeaways.text: Scores revenue rose 33% to $414M — driven by a higher unit price for mortgage-origination scores, which more than offset lower mortgage volumes. B2B scoring revenue rose 39%.

takeaways.title: Underlying EPS is much higher
takeaways.text: Excluding the settlement accrual, the restructuring charge and the investment gain, non-GAAP EPS was $11.10 versus $8.12 on a GAAP basis — and non-GAAP net income rose 28% to $239M.

takeaways.title: Platform software is compounding
takeaways.text: Software platform ARR grew 72% with a 156% dollar-based net retention rate, even as older non-platform software shrank 18% — the mix shift FICO has been pushing for.

oneTimers: A $65M accrual for a proposed settlement of the antitrust class-action lawsuits over the Scores business sits inside SG&A this quarter.
A $27M restructuring charge for a committed workforce-reduction plan is shown as its own running-cost line.
A $47.9M non-operating gain on the sale of a minority equity investment is inside other income (expense).
FICO gave no FY27 guidance, citing its transition to bespoke mortgage-score pricing and an uncertain mortgage market.
